scenes.text: Standard databases find exact matches. Vector databases find similar ones — and that changes everything.
Every item — text, image, audio — gets converted into a list of numbers called an embedding. Similar items cluster nearby in that high-dimensional space.
Brute-force comparison across millions of vectors is too slow. So vector databases build specialized indexes — like HNSW — that skip most of the space and jump straight to the nearest neighbors.
That's what powers semantic search, RAG pipelines, and recommendations. Not matching keywords — matching meaning.
